I farm 9 mu, and I do not start from zero. I start from what has worked here in Quzhou County, then I adjust a little for cost, water, and yield. Since I have well irrigation and I know this land well after 45 years, I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is still the safest income on my farm. I will put 6 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same 6 mu, and I will keep 3 mu in cotton. I have high school education, so I do think about nutrient balance, not only habit. Wheat takes the bigger fertilizer bill because if wheat is weak before winter or at jointing, I lose yield fast. Maize after wheat will go mostly with no-tillage and machine sowing, because that saves labor and catches the summer moisture. Cotton is slower and needs more watching for insects, so I will not expand it too much on a 2-person household. I would rather spend a little extra on fertilizer than watch the yield fall, but I still count every yuan, so I will keep the rates close to what gives steady output on our kind of land with irrigation.
